If an artwork is vault-sworn to a museum.why: "Vault-sworn" is a made-up relation (catalogued as vault_sworn_to, fictional, no property tags); nobody uses the phrase and it has no default reading about whether it carries from a museum to its city. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

Claude Monet was a French painter..why: Stated in the first sentence of Wikipedia's biography; 'Claude Monet was a French painter' has 137 exact hits.

Leo Tolstoy wrote Don Quixote..why: False: Don Quixote is by Miguel de Cervantes.

sources.quote: Don Quixote is a novel by Miguel de Cervantes, written in Early Modern Spanish and published in two parts in 1605 and 1615.

The Uffizi Gallery is in Florence..why: The first sentence of the Uffizi article places it in Florence; a museum's city is the first thing said about it.

sources.quote: The Uffizi Gallery is an art museum adjacent to the Piazza della Signoria in the Historic Centre of Florence in the region of Tuscany, Italy.

The Prado Museum is in Madrid..why: The first sentence of the Prado article places it in central Madrid.

sources.quote: The Museo del Prado, officially known as Museo Nacional del Prado, is the main Spanish national art museum, located in central Madrid.

notes: RBox expansion paired with literature_arts-replace-0017 (which gives the chain housed_in o located_in a new target): a made-up relation, vault_sworn_to (artwork to museum), is given the chain vault_sworn_to o located_in -> vault_sworn_to, applied to real artworks and museums. The museum-in-city hop is left out of the prompt (README, Role chains through real knowledge) and is a real fact with a check. The pairings are made up and none matches where the work actually hangs, so the answers are fixed by the edit alone. Side facts and near and far unrelated queries are those of the revision record. Yes and no are balanced: the direct question and the first instance (yes), the second instance asks whether it could be otherwise (no).
